teaching_note: Start with a framework-neutral contract: authorized → reading → checking → awaiting-review → accepted-local, with paused, rejected and cancelled exits. Every transition carries run/task ID, input version, accepted sources, pending work and decision owner; no graph edge grants a tool permission. A fixed policy packet can use a deterministic graph; adaptive next-passage selection is a separate behavior to justify and evaluate. [@scholarly_anthropic_building_effective_agents]
title: LangChain/LangGraph: State Machine Orchestration

teaching_note: Expression-style composition connects an upstream output to a downstream input; that interface needs a schema and failure contract even when a library makes chaining concise. In the local exercise, read returns passage IDs, check consumes only those IDs, and draft rejects uncited assertions; exact LCEL syntax and installed-version behavior remain unverified here rather than being inferred from the inherited heading.
title: LCEL: LangChain Expression Language

teaching_note: Cycles need explicit progress and exit conditions, not just a maximum conversation length. A synthetic checking state with missing R1 may try one approved alternative passage, then becomes paused/unsupported; restoring checkpoint K0 requires its corpus and policy versions rather than assuming persisted state is safe to resume. Library checkpoint, cancellation and interrupt guarantees require directly checked versioned documentation and are unknown in this lesson's source packet.
title: LangGraph: Stateful, Cyclical Agentic Workflows

teaching_note: A trace explains which proposed steps, permission decisions and observations produced a draft; it is not itself prevention or independent audit storage. For synthetic event E1 retain run Q1/task T1, local_read, record reference R1§2, allow/H1 and outcome observed, while keeping source text separately; verify trace access, retention and immutability instead of indiscriminately logging raw parameters.
title: LangSmith: Observability and Tracing

teaching_note: Role-based collaboration is useful when distinct deliverables can be checked independently, not merely when several agents can speak. A provider homepage or practitioner overview supplies product context, not evidence that the crew is more reliable, isolated or efficient than a single fixed workflow.
title: CrewAI: Role-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration

raw: 33.2.1 Crew, Agent, Task, and Process Objects
teaching_note: Distinguish the group being coordinated, the worker assigned, the task's required output and the scheduling process. The framework-neutral task contract is T1: read R1/R3 under H1, return status/passages and unresolved currency; an 'agent' object alone does not specify its authority, acceptance criteria or evidence sources. Exact class names and constructor contracts are version-dependent and not established here.
title: Crew, Agent, Task, and Process Objects

raw: 33.2.2 Sequential, Parallel, and Hierarchical Process Modes
teaching_note: Sequential scheduling fits dependent tasks, parallel scheduling fits disjoint reads, and hierarchical scheduling adds parent-child aggregation. These are architecture alternatives, not a claim that every named framework exposes equivalent APIs or modes; shared origins and shared contaminated memory can defeat apparent independence under all three.
title: Sequential, Parallel, and Hierarchical Process Modes

teaching_note: A catalog entry establishes that an adapter may be available, not that its dependencies, access or intended use are approved. The local exercise permits only a packet-reader adapter; an installed outbound adapter remains denied and may not be substituted when a read fails. Record the actual enforcement point rather than inferring it from a framework's tool ecosystem.
title: Built-in Tool Ecosystem

teaching_note: Conversation orchestration selects who receives which message and when; it does not make that message trusted or factually supported. Keep source passages, proposals, validation decisions and human approvals as distinct record types so a conversational reply cannot silently become a permission grant.
title: AutoGen (Microsoft): Multi-Agent Conversation Patterns

In the neutral contract, the assistant proposes draft D1-v1 and the mediator can route a review request, but only the named owner's recorded decision can accept that exact version for local use.
title: AssistantAgent and UserProxyAgent Pattern

raw: 33.3.2 GroupChat with RoundRobin and AutoSelect Managers
teaching_note: Round-robin selection offers predictable turns, whereas content-based selection introduces another choice whose failure cases must be evaluated. Neither selection method establishes evidence independence or authority; stop after the fixed classroom turn budget and retain unresolved dissent rather than allowing the manager to manufacture consensus. Exact manager names and semantics remain source-guide context until checked against a pinned release.
title: GroupChat with RoundRobin and AutoSelect Managers

raw: 33.3.3 Code Execution Risk and Sandboxing Requirements[^147]

title: Code Execution Risk and Sandboxing Requirements

title: Basic Reasoning Agents

raw: 33.5.2 Tool-Based Agents (Function Calling and MCP Servers)
teaching_note: Function schemas describe arguments and results; protocol servers expose capabilities; the host must still enforce the exact operation, resource and actor scope. In a local stand-in, a schema-valid read of R9 is denied when H1 permits only R1–R5; no server description or successful capability negotiation enlarges H1. [@official_model_context_protocol_specification]
title: Tool-Based Agents (Function Calling and MCP Servers)

teaching_note: Screen-based interaction can make one apparent action trigger several hidden state changes, so visual access is not a narrow permission contract. Review only supplied fictional screenshots and proposed actions here: a button labeled 'share' is identified as excluded outbound activity and not clicked; a screenshot's text never authorizes navigation or submission.
title: Computer-Use Agents

teaching_note: Distinguish proposing a source change, reviewing its diff, executing it and deploying it; each is a different action with different consequences. The local teaching artifact is a supplied diff and evidence record, not permission to install dependencies or run generated code; a plausible explanation cannot substitute for observed behavior under authorized verification.
title: Coding Agents

teaching_note: Speech interfaces add transcription, speaker attribution and timing uncertainty to the ordinary evidence contract. A supplied synthetic transcript saying 'review not required' with an uncertain negation span must remain uncertain until the approved recording is checked; neither perceived voice identity nor conversational fluency authenticates an instruction.
title: Speech-to-Speech Agents

teaching_note: A supervisor selects children, parallel tasks share a join, and a subgraph packages a bounded internal workflow; these are compositional choices with different cancellation and partial-result needs. If one child fails, the join must expose incomplete dependencies rather than silently replace its output, and cancelling the parent must revoke all outstanding child grants.
title: Orchestration Patterns: Supervisor, Parallel, Subgraph

teaching_note: A message format can support interoperability without guaranteeing permission inheritance, factual support or safe recovery. Completed synthetic handoff: run Q1, parent T0, child T1 complete on corpus P1-v1; accepted R1§2, rejected-as-current R3, claim C1 depends on R1, T2 lineage pending, scope local-read-only until K1, approval absent, next owner Instructor-B. Instructor-B holds final acceptance pending T2 and a version-bound review; T1 cannot redelegate, send externally or turn a pending field into a completed result. [@official_agent2agent_protocol_specification]
title: Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Protocols: Interoperability Between Frameworks
